pharm: A thioxanthene typical antipsychotic (the cis(Z)-isomer of clopenthixol) available as oral tablets, a short-acting injection (acetate, 'Acuphase') and a long-acting depot (decanoate); it produces antipsychotic and sedative effects primarily by blocking dopamine D1 and D2 receptors, with additional alpha-adrenergic, histaminergic, and serotonergic antagonism.
quick: Oral 20-60 mg/day (max ~150 mg); depot decanoate 200-400 mg every 2-4 weeks
May be taken with or without food
Avoid unless essential; neonatal EPS/withdrawal in 3rd trimester
Small amounts in milk; use with caution / avoid
Caution; reduce dose / monitor in hepatic impairment
Avoid - additive sedation and CNS depression
EPS, sedation, ECG/QT, metabolic parameters, prolactin
summary: Zuclopenthixol is a thioxanthene typical (first-generation) antipsychotic used to treat schizophrenia and other psychoses, including the management of agitation, aggression, and acute psychotic episodes. It is the active cis(Z)-isomer of clopenthixol and is available as oral tablets, a short-acting acetate injection (zuclopenthixol acetate, used for acute psychotic exacerbation with effect over 2-3 days) and a long-acting decanoate depot for maintenance. It acts mainly by blocking dopamine D1/D2 receptors, with sedative properties from antihistaminic and alpha-adrenergic actions. Like other typical antipsychotics it can cause extrapyramidal side effects, sedation, anticholinergic effects, QT prolongation, hyperprolactinemia, weight gain, and rarely neuroleptic malignant syndrome and tardive dyskinesia. It is not FDA-approved; dosing and warnings follow the European SmPC and BNF.
indications: Treatment of schizophrenia and other psychoses, particularly with agitation, aggression, or hostility (oral and depot)
Short-term management of acute psychosis, mania, or exacerbations of chronic psychosis (zuclopenthixol acetate, 'Acuphase')
Maintenance treatment of chronic schizophrenia and related psychoses (zuclopenthixol decanoate depot)

dosage.d: Initial 20-30 mg/day in divided doses; maintenance usually 20-50 mg/day; up to ~150 mg/day if needed
50-150 mg, repeated if needed after 2-3 days; max 4 injections / 400 mg over a course not exceeding ~2 weeks
dosage.n: Not for rapid initial control of very acutely disturbed patients within minutes; not for long-term use

dosage.d: Test dose 100 mg, then 200-400 mg every 2-4 weeks (higher in some patients up to ~600 mg)
dosage.n: Adjust dose and interval to response

dosage.d: Use lower starting doses (e.g., quarter to half the usual)
dosage.n: Greater sensitivity to EPS, sedation, and hypotension

admin: Oral tablets may be taken with or without food; divide the daily dose as prescribed
Zuclopenthixol acetate (Acuphase) is given by deep intramuscular injection for short-term management only - it is not for emergency immediate control and not for maintenance
Zuclopenthixol decanoate depot is given by deep intramuscular injection into the gluteal muscle (or lateral thigh); start with a test dose to assess tolerance before full dosing
Rotate depot injection sites and use proper deep IM (Z-track) technique; volumes above ~2 mL should be split between sites
Titrate gradually, monitor for extrapyramidal effects and sedation, and avoid combining the acetate and decanoate concepts (different durations of action)
moa: Zuclopenthixol is the pharmacologically active cis(Z)-isomer of the thioxanthene clopenthixol. Its antipsychotic action results primarily from blockade of postsynaptic dopamine receptors (both D1 and D2 subtypes) in mesolimbic and mesocortical pathways, reducing positive psychotic symptoms; D2 blockade in the nigrostriatal and tuberoinfundibular pathways accounts for extrapyramidal effects and hyperprolactinemia. It also antagonizes alpha-1 adrenergic receptors (causing sedation and orthostatic hypotension), histamine H1 receptors (sedation, weight gain), and to a lesser extent 5-HT2 and muscarinic receptors. The decanoate ester in an oily vehicle is slowly hydrolyzed after IM injection to release active drug over weeks, while the acetate ester provides an intermediate duration of action over 2-3 days.

absolute: Comatose states or acute CNS depression (including from alcohol, barbiturates, or opioids)
Known hypersensitivity to zuclopenthixol or thioxanthenes
Pheochromocytoma (for related thioxanthenes) and acute intoxicated states
relative: Cardiovascular disease, QT prolongation, or electrolyte disturbance
Parkinson's disease and other movement disorders
Elderly with dementia-related psychosis (increased mortality - class effect)
Narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy, or paralytic ileus (anticholinergic effects)
monitor: Metabolic parameters (weight, glucose, lipids) and prolactin

preg: Avoid during pregnancy unless essential. Neonates exposed to antipsychotics in the third trimester are at risk of extrapyramidal and withdrawal symptoms (agitation, hypertonia/hypotonia, tremor, somnolence, feeding/breathing difficulty) after delivery; monitor the newborn. Use the lowest effective dose if treatment is needed.
lact: Zuclopenthixol passes into breast milk in small amounts. Because of potential effects on the infant, use with caution and generally avoid breastfeeding, or monitor the infant if treatment is essential.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment; consider lower starting doses and careful titration, as accumulation and increased sensitivity to adverse effects may occur.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment, as the drug is hepatically metabolized; reduce the dose, titrate slowly, and monitor for excessive sedation and adverse effects.

major: Other QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., class IA/III antiarrhythmics, other antipsychotics, certain antibiotics) - additive risk of QT prolongation and arrhythmia
CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines, anesthetics) - enhanced sedation and respiratory/CNS depression
moderate: Anticholinergic drugs - additive anticholinergic effects and may worsen tardive dyskinesia
Levodopa and dopamine agonists - mutual antagonism (reduced effect of both)
Drugs lowering the seizure threshold - increased seizure risk
Metoclopramide and other dopamine antagonists - additive extrapyramidal effects
minor: Enzyme inducers/inhibitors may alter zuclopenthixol levels (metabolized via CYP2D6 among others)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - it markedly increases sedation and central nervous system depression.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate serum prolactin and can affect ECG (QT); monitor ECG and metabolic/prolactin parameters as appropriate.

emergency: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (high fever, rigidity, autonomic instability, altered consciousness)
Serious arrhythmia / syncope from QT prolongation

monitoring: Extrapyramidal symptoms and emergence of tardive dyskinesia
ECG and QT interval, especially with cardiac risk or other QT-prolonging drugs
Weight, blood glucose, and lipids (metabolic monitoring)
Prolactin if symptoms occur; full blood count if infection/fever; liver function as indicated
Mental state and response to treatment
counsel: Take your tablets exactly as prescribed; do not stop suddenly without advice as symptoms can return
This medicine can make you drowsy - do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you, and avoid alcohol
Get up slowly from sitting or lying to avoid dizziness
Report muscle stiffness, restlessness, unusual movements of the face/tongue, or shaking
Seek urgent help for high fever with muscle stiffness and confusion, fainting, or a fast/irregular heartbeat
Tell your team about all other medicines, and keep your follow-up appointments for blood and heart checks (especially for depot injections)
pk: Oral antipsychotic effect over days; acetate injection acts over 2-3 days
Oral plasma Tmax ~4 hours; acetate IM peak ~24-48 hours; decanoate depot peak ~4-7 days
Oral ~20 hours; decanoate depot apparent half-life ~17-19 days
Acetate ~2-3 days; decanoate depot ~2-4 weeks per injection
Store below 25 C, protect from light; do not freeze injections
pearls: Three formulations with very different durations: oral, acetate ('Acuphase', effect over 2-3 days for short-term use), and decanoate depot (every 2-4 weeks for maintenance) - do not confuse them
Zuclopenthixol acetate is NOT for instant tranquilization of an acutely disturbed patient and is not for maintenance
Give a depot test dose first to assess tolerability before full maintenance dosing
Typical antipsychotic - watch for extrapyramidal symptoms, tardive dyskinesia, QT prolongation, hyperprolactinemia, and neuroleptic malignant syndrome
Increased mortality when used for dementia-related psychosis in the elderly (antipsychotic class warning)
Not FDA-approved - dosing and safety follow the EMA SmPC and BNF
missed: For oral therapy, if you miss a dose take it as soon as you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it - do not double up. For depot injections, contact your clinic to reschedule a missed dose as soon as possible.
overdose: Overdose features include drowsiness, coma, extrapyramidal symptoms, convulsions, hypotension or shock, hyper- or hypothermia, and arrhythmias (including QT prolongation). There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with airway/ventilatory support, cardiovascular monitoring and support, treatment of seizures and arrhythmias, and use of anticholinergics or supportive measures for extrapyramidal reactions. Avoid adrenaline (epinephrine) for hypotension because of paradoxical further blood-pressure fall.
